questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The development, launch and early reception of the original Macintosh
How the Xerox Alto's custom processor was built and marketed
Microsoft's rivalry with Apple over graphical operating systems
The history of the Apple II line and its eventual discontinuation
questions.explain: It covers the Mac's development, 1984 debut and hardware.

questions.q: Who directed the "1984" commercial that introduced the Macintosh?
options: Steve Jobs
John Sculley
Ridley Scott
Regis McKenna
questions.explain: It was a US$1.5 million Ridley Scott commercial.

questions.q: Which two applications were bundled with the Macintosh at launch?
options: MultiPlan and Word
MacWrite and MacPaint
Lisa Write and Lisa Draw
QuickDraw and Alto
questions.explain: It came bundled with MacWrite and MacPaint to show off its interface.

questions.q: What happened with the "Test Drive a Macintosh" promotion?
options: Only 20,000 people took part, and dealers praised it as a sales driver
It was cancelled before launch after Apple lacked enough demo machines
Returned machines were refurbished and resold at a profit to schools nationwide
200,000 took part, but dealers disliked it and returned units were unsellable
questions.explain: Dealers disliked it, supply was short and many returns were in bad condition.

questions.q: Why did the Mac initially lack software?
options: Apple barred outside developers from writing programs for it until 1985, a year after launch
Text-mode applications had to be rewritten for the GUI, which many developers declined to do
Its small ROM left no room for any programs beyond the two bundled applications
Microsoft refused to support the platform and withheld its office software for years
questions.explain: The OS was designed largely for the GUI, so existing apps needed time-consuming rewrites.
